key_insight: Low-cost spindle and axis current signals can detect groove-defect formation in friction stir welding about 10 s before the defect becomes visibly apparent.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical real-time quality monitoring for CNC-based FSW using sensors already available on industrial machines, reducing added hardware cost and complexity.
method: Segment machine current signals from defect-free, defective, and transient weld regions.
Apply FFT, power spectral density, and spectral coherence analysis to identify signature changes.
Use spindle current coherence at the fundamental frequency and harmonics as the primary defect indicator.
evidence_signal: Defect-free regions showed high spectral coherence, while defective regions showed a marked coherence drop at the spindle fundamental frequency and harmonics, consistent with XCT-confirmed subsurface discontinuities.
watch_item: Performance was demonstrated on a specific AA2139/AA7075 lap-joint case, so broader transferability to other alloys, tools, and machine setups should be validated.
paper_title: Early detection of groove defect in friction stir welding through data-driven process monitoring
